harvestMonths.notes: Annual shoot cutting for processing, not flower or fresh-fruit picking.

yearsToFirstCrop.notes: First commercial cutting readiness at 12–18 months in the described Cape production system. The account discusses sowing and transfer to plantations but does not explicitly define whether the clock starts at sowing or planting out. Confirm starting stock and timing locally. This is tea-shoot establishment, not fruit-tree bearing.

supplementaryReferences.title: Commercial tea cutting cycle and product
supplementaryReferences.note: Selected commercial rooibos forms in the Cederberg winter-rainfall region are cut annually December–April, retaining older branches. Cut shoots are chopped, bruised, oxidised and dried. Fresh shoot kg and dried tea kg are separate products. The account describes replacement after up to five harvest years, not a mature kg/plant curve.

productionGuidance.products: young shoots for dried rooibos tea
care: Match planting to acidic, sandy winter-rainfall soils and locally suitable rooibos forms.
Keep fresh-cut shoot weights separate from processed dried tea; record the actual processing output.
purchase: Ask a local rooibos nursery or adviser for correctly identified, locally proven planting material. The Cape cycle is not a nationwide tea forecast.
